description: ODC (T coverage): REST consumed with a STRUCTURE INSIDE A STRUCTURE, which the ODC lane had never proven. Mirrors tests/jobs/rest-query-nested.json: a GET to frankfurter.app whose response is {amount, base, date, rates:{USD}} - that is, one attribute of the response structure is itself a structure. The rule is the same in both lanes: the CHILD structure is created first and then its NAME is used as the DataType of the parent's attribute; the kernel resolves the name to the record type. The query string has no op of its own - it is written in the URLPath (/latest?from={from}&to={to}) and each {param} asks for an IRestActionInput in UrlPlacement. In the end a shareable server action calls the method and reads TWO levels deep in a single expression (GetLatest.Response.Rates.USD), which is the proof that the nesting really exists in the model and not only in the JSON. ONE platform difference showed up and is measured in the _why of the usages: in ODC that expression counts as a consumer of the nested structure (real=3), in the O11 lane it does not (real=2).

expectedMessages.why: ODC: an app (CrossDevice) does not expose a public server action (the live Studio errors); the action stays private and without a consumer in this proof job

ops.name: WfNstRates
ops._why: the CHILD structure is born first: the DataType of the parent's attribute is resolved by NAME, so the name has to exist already when the parent is written
NameInJSON is independent of the attribute name: the JSON comes in lowercase and the model keeps the OutSystems name
HERE is the point of the job: the DataType is not a primitive type, it is the NAME of the IRestStructure created above - structure inside structure
the query string has NO op of its own: it is written in the URLPath and each {param} asks for an input in UrlPlacement
a consumed REST method is called like any server action; the NAME OF THE NODE (GetLatest) is what serves as the prefix in the expression, not the name of the method
a text literal in an argument carries quotes inside the JSON: the property is an OutSystems expression, not text
PROOF of the nesting: three hops in a single expression - output of the node, record attribute of the response structure and attribute of the child structure
proves the URLPath with the query string and the HTTPMethod
proves the nested attribute: DataType is the structure WfNstRates, not a primitive

proves the TWO structures side by side inside the same IRestClient: the nesting is not a structure inside the tree of the other - they are siblings, and what links them is the DataType of the attribute. That is why the dump of the parent alone would never show the USD

MEASURED PLATFORM DIFFERENCE: in ODC the child structure has real=3 - the IRestStructureAttribute of the parent, the IAttribute of the 'WfNstRates Record' (the IAnonymousStructure that the platform creates by itself, the same in both lanes) AND the ITextBasedExpression 'GetLatest.Response.Rates.USD' itself; the same job in the O11 lane gives real=2, because there the expression that crosses the second level does NOT count as a consumer of the structure. Practical consequence: a delete of the nested structure is refused in ODC because of the expression and would not be refused because of it in SS11
proves the flow that reads the two levels and returns the Rate
